claim.pdf_says: Figure D.1 draws one tall brace "}" on the right-hand side of the flowchart. That single brace spans ALL THREE exit arrows -- the arrow leaving imperative-statement-1, the arrow leaving imperative-statement-2 and the arrow leaving imperative-statement-3 -- and the footnote reference "**" is printed to the right of the brace, vertically centred beside it. The footnote itself (page 1064) reads: "**   Each of these control transfers is to the end of the SEARCH statement unless the flow of control of the imperative-statement contains an EXIT, GO TO, GOBACK, or RETURN statement."
claim.markdown_says: Condition-1 → True → imperative-statement-2 → **\*\***  (the brace is not rendered at all; the "**" marker appears only at the end of the imperative-statement-2 row, and the imperative-statement-1 row reads "→ True (AT END) * → imperative-statement-1 →" and the imperative-statement-3 row reads "\* Condition-2 → True → imperative-statement-3 * →", neither carrying "**")
claim.why_it_matters: The brace is the only thing that makes footnote ** apply to all three control transfers. With the brace dropped and "**" attached to a single row, the plural antecedent of "Each of these control transfers" disappears: a reader of the markdown concludes that only the imperative-statement-2 exit transfers to the end of the SEARCH statement, and that the AT END exit and the second WHEN exit are governed by something else. That is exactly the falsely-restrictive reading this sweep is looking for, applied to a figure grouping delimiter rather than a bracket.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct render at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1063/spec_p1063.png) plus a 2x crop of the right-hand third of the figure (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1063/my_brace_zoom.png). What I actually see printed on the page: a single tall right curly brace whose upper terminal sits above the imperative-statement-1 exit arrow and whose lower terminal sits below the imperative-statement-3 exit arrow, with its centre cusp at the imperative-statement-2 row. All three horizontal exit arrows (one from each imperative-statement box) run rightward and terminate at that one brace. The glyph pair '**' is printed to the right of the brace, vertically centred on the cusp -- i.e. it labels the BRACE, not the imperative-statement-2 row. It is a grouping delimiter with a group label, not decoration.

The markdown transcription (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 42575-42619; extract at E:/Temp/specrecon/v1063/page-1063.md) contains no brace, no group, and no note that the three exits converge. It emits the three rows as independent lines:
  line 26: '→ True (AT END) * → imperative-statement-1 →'
  line 30: 'Condition-1 → True → imperative-statement-2 → **\*\***'
  line 34: '\* Condition-2 → True → imperative-statement-3 * →'
Only the middle row carries the '**'. Both quotations in the claim are verbatim-accurate, including the odd '**\*\***' bold-wrapped escaping, which renders as a bold '**'. The transcription error is explainable: the '**' is vertically centred at the statement-2 row, so a line-oriented reader binds it to that row's text run and the brace vector art is dropped entirely.

I also verified the footnote quotation. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 42631 (page 1064) reads exactly: '\*\* Each of these control transfers is to the end of the SEARCH statement unless the flow of control of the imperative-statement contains an EXIT, GO TO, GOBACK, or RETURN statement.' The plural 'Each of these control transfers' is now stranded with exactly one visible referent, which is incoherent on its face and unrecoverable: nothing in the markdown tells the reader which set of transfers the footnote scopes over.

I tried and failed to refute this on the usual grounds. (a) Not reflow or an adjacent line -- I read the whole page-1063 block and the whole page-1064 block; no brace character, no 'these three', no grouping prose anywhere. (b) Not page-break furniture or formatting -- a brace that binds three arrows to one footnote is content in a flowchart the same way a bracket is content in a general format. (c) Not a misquote -- both sides quote correctly. (d) The meaning does change: under the markdown the AT END exit and the second WHEN exit lose their stated post-completion destination, and a reader could plausibly infer that after imperative-statement-1 completes control does NOT go to the end of the SEARCH statement (e.g. that it falls through into the WHEN tests). That is the falsely-restrictive scope loss the sweep targets.

One honest mitigation on IMPACT, which does not change real=true: Annex D is informative (the page itself says 'This figure is not intended to dictate implementation'), and the same behaviour is stated normatively and correctly in the transcribed general rules of 14.9.37 SEARCH -- specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30534 for imperative-statement-1 ('upon completion of the execution of imperative-statement-1, control is transferred to the end of the SEARCH statement') and line 30530 for imperative-statement-2. So an implementer who reads the normative text is not misled, and no compiler behaviour is at risk from this alone. Severity 'structural' is correct as a description of the transcription defect (a lost grouping delimiter that reassigns a footnote's scope); it would be an overstatement to call it a conformance risk.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as stated, with two refinements. (1) Placement: the brace's centre cusp -- not merely the brace as a whole -- is level with the imperative-statement-2 row, and '**' is printed to the right of that cusp; this is why the transcription bound '**' to the statement-2 text run and dropped the brace. (2) Scope of harm: the figure is in informative Annex D and the identical rule survives correctly in the transcribed normative general rules of 14.9.37 SEARCH (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 30530 and 30534), so no implementable semantics is lost from the document as a whole. The defect is a genuine, meaning-changing loss of a figure grouping delimiter -- the brace binding all three imperative-statement exit arrows into one group labelled '**' is absent, leaving the plural 'Each of these control transfers' with a single visible referent -- but it is a transcription-fidelity defect, not a conformance hazard. Fix: render the group in the markdown, e.g. emit the three exit rows followed by a line such as 'All three of the above control transfers are grouped by a brace labelled ** ' (or attach '**' to each of the three rows), so the footnote's plural antecedent is recoverable.
